title: Culture and Economy
lines: This topic covers Pakistan's national symbols, languages, heritage sites, crops, minerals and industries. USAT asks short factual questions, so learn the tables. Figures such as output or population change from year to year; the test avoids them, and so should your revision.
## National symbols
| Symbol | Fact
| National language | Urdu (English is also used for official purposes)
| National anthem | lyrics by Hafeez Jalandhari, music by Ahmed G. Chagla; approved in 1954
| National flag | dark green with a white band at the hoist; crescent and star; adopted on 11 August 1947
| National poet | Allama Muhammad Iqbal
| National animal | markhor
| National bird | chukar partridge
| National tree | deodar
| National flower | jasmine (chambeli)
| National fruit | mango
| National dress | shalwar kameez
| Motto | Faith, Unity, Discipline (Iman, Ittehad, Nazm)
- On the flag, green stands for the Muslim majority and white for religious minorities. The crescent stands for progress and the star for light and knowledge.
## Languages
- Urdu is the national language and the main link language. Punjabi is the most widely spoken mother tongue.
- Other major languages: Pashto (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa), Sindhi (Sindh), Balochi and Brahui (Balochistan), Saraiki (southern Punjab), Hindko, Shina and Balti in the north.
## Heritage sites (UNESCO World Heritage)
| Site | Province | Note
| Mohenjo-daro | Sindh | Indus Valley city; the Great Bath
| Taxila | Punjab | Gandhara centre of Buddhist learning
| Takht-i-Bahi and Sahr-i-Bahlol | Khyber Pakhtunkhwa | Buddhist monastery ruins
| Makli monuments, Thatta | Sindh | one of the largest graveyards in the world
| Lahore Fort and Shalimar Gardens | Punjab | Mughal; the gardens built by Shah Jahan
| Rohtas Fort | Punjab | built by Sher Shah Suri near Jhelum
Other landmarks: Harappa (Punjab), Badshahi Mosque, Lahore (built by Aurangzeb), Faisal Mosque, Islamabad, Minar-e-Pakistan, Lahore, and the Mazar-e-Quaid, Karachi.
## Poets, saints and literature
| Figure | Language or place | Remember
| Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai | Sindhi | Shah Jo Risalo; shrine at Bhit Shah
| Waris Shah | Punjabi | the verse romance Heer
| Bulleh Shah | Punjabi | Sufi poet buried at Kasur
| Khushal Khan Khattak | Pashto | warrior-poet
| Rahman Baba | Pashto | Sufi poet of Peshawar
| Data Ganj Bakhsh (Ali Hujwiri) | Lahore | author of Kashf al-Mahjub
| Lal Shahbaz Qalandar | Sehwan, Sindh | famous Sufi shrine

- Cultural events include the Shandur Polo Festival, played on one of the world's highest polo grounds between Chitral and Gilgit teams. Lok Virsa in Islamabad preserves folk heritage, music and crafts.
## Agriculture
| Season | Sown | Crops
| Rabi | autumn and winter, harvested in spring | wheat, gram, barley, mustard
| Kharif | summer, harvested in autumn | rice, cotton, sugarcane, maize
- Wheat is the staple food. Cotton feeds the textile industry, the largest manufacturing sector and the main export earner.
- Sargodha is famous for citrus (kinnow); Multan and the Sindh belt for mangoes.
## Minerals and energy
| Resource | Where
| Natural gas | Sui, Balochistan (discovered 1952)
| Rock salt | Khewra, Salt Range
| Lignite coal | Thar, Sindh
| Copper and gold | Saindak and Reko Diq, Chagai, Balochistan
| Hydropower | Tarbela and Mangla dams
## Industries and cities
| City | Known for
| Faisalabad | textiles (the Manchester of Pakistan)
| Sialkot | sports goods and surgical instruments
| Gujranwala | metal and electrical goods
| Karachi | port, steel (Pakistan Steel Mills), finance
| Gujrat | ceramics and fans
| Hyderabad | bangles
- The State Bank of Pakistan is the central bank. It was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam on 1 July 1948.
> Which crop is sown in the rabi season?  (A) rice  (B) cotton  (C) wheat  (D) sugarcane
> C. Wheat is sown in winter and harvested in spring. The others are kharif crops.
> The Shalimar Gardens in Lahore were laid out by  (A) Akbar  (B) Shah Jahan  (C) Aurangzeb  (D) Jahangir
> B. Shah Jahan also built the Taj Mahal; Aurangzeb built the Badshahi Mosque.
## Traps
! White on the flag represents minorities, not peace.
! Rohtas Fort was built by Sher Shah Suri, not a Mughal emperor.
! Urdu is the national language; Punjabi has the most native speakers. The two facts are not in conflict.
## Quick check
- Markhor, chukar, deodar, jasmine, mango.
- Anthem: Hafeez Jalandhari (words), Ahmed G. Chagla (music).
- Six UNESCO sites: Mohenjo-daro, Taxila, Takht-i-Bahi, Makli, Lahore Fort with Shalimar, Rohtas.
- Rabi wheat; kharif rice, cotton, sugarcane, maize.
